citation.title: GANTL: Towards Practical and Real-Time Topology Optimization with Conditional GANs and Transfer Learning
citation.authors: Mohammad Mahdi Behzadi, Horea T. Ilies

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For seen boundary conditions with one force, GANTL outputs differ from SIMP designs by 1.00% average compliance error and 2.12% image MSE across the tested mesh sizes.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No paired classical versus GANTL run times or numeric speed-up are reported; the introduction cites 1.85 s per SIMP iteration from a prior paper on a different problem.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and introduction claim real-time design exploration qualitatively; Tables 3-5 report larger compliance errors for unseen boundary and loading conditions.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP for training and test ground truth (Sections 3.4, 4.1)
baseline.implementation: freely available MATLAB code cited as the 88-line SIMP code, modified for automatic case generation (Section 4.1)
baseline.hardware_classical: UConn HPC facility, Red Hat RHEL7; method-specific hardware not stated (Section 3.5)
baseline.hardware_ml: UConn HPC facility, Red Hat RHEL7; method-specific hardware not stated (Section 3.5)
baseline.classical_iterations: not stated for own experiments; introduction cites hundreds of iterations in prior SIMP work
baseline.classical_time: not stated for own experiments; introduction cites 1.85 s per iteration for a 300 x 100 MMB beam from prior work
baseline.ml_time: not stated numerically; real-time prediction claimed (abstract and introduction)
baseline.training_time: not stated numerically; topology-aware loss said to increase training time (Section 4.2)
baseline.data_generation_cost: 11,000 low-resolution cases plus 1,500 high-resolution cases generated with SIMP; time cost not stated here (Sections 3.4, 4.1, 5)
baseline.quality_metric: compliance error, image MSE, binary accuracy (Section 3.5, Tables 2-5)
baseline.quality_gap: seen BC/one force: 1.00% mean compliance error; unseen BC/one force: 7.74%; seen BC/two forces: 10.48% (Tables 2-4)

R1.evidence: Section 4.2, Table 2: primary quantitative comparison is compliance quality, with no paired speed timing.

R2.evidence: Section 4.2, Table 2: no classical versus GANTL timing forms the primary outcome.

R3.evidence: Section 4.2, Table 2: primary outcome is design-quality error, not a quantified speed claim.

R4.evidence: Section 3.5 and Tables 2-5: returned outputs are assigned compliance errors against SIMP, but no volume-violation or disconnected-output rate is reported; the text notes connectivity problems.

reporting.n_test_cases: Tables 2-5: 7,473 seen-BC/one-force 40 x 80 tests and smaller sets by mesh and scenario; counts stated per row

notes: The paper uses SIMP results as a classical comparator, but the first quantitative GANTL-to-SIMP outcome is quality error in Section 4.2. Real-time speed statements are qualitative, without model inference times.
